region_scene_page.compact: A stripped 1950s guitar-and-slapback lane where country boogie, blues, R&B, and hillbilly flash become urgent rock records.
region_scene_page.standard: Rockabilly came out of small labels, Southern studios, young players, and quick takes that prized feel over polish. Sun Records is the best-known center, but the vocabulary spreads through Carl Perkins, Gene Vincent, Johnny Burnette, Eddie Cochran, Duane Eddy, Link Wray, and other records that make guitar attitude the event. Compared with broader early rock, this lane feels more wiry and local: slapped bass, echo, hiccuped vocals, lean drums, sharp guitar breaks, and very little orchestral cushion.
